## Claude review (read-only) — subject `f441fab10e7254af12ce56a3402a5de5fbad655e`

This report belongs to the existing claim `a11036a6-b143-4701-8c09-b1b2d30e44dc`; nothing was re-claimed. `submit` with the trusted CLI on main `b062de332` failed three times, and each time no state was persisted (status still `comment-running`):
- `github-read-failed` (operation read, no HTTP status, diagnostic unknown);
- `Native required checks are not passing` (while every check was green);
- `github-read-failed` again.

The claim itself returned `state-write-uncertain` but did persist. The durable ledger `.codex-bug-state.json` on `codex/bug-control` is now **4,308,430 bytes** (`encoding: none`; read through the blob path as about 5.7 MB of base64 per load). That is under `MAX_DURABLE_STATE_BYTES` (8 MiB) but large enough that reads look like they are intermittently timing out. As agreed, the actual report is published here for Codex to reconcile on this claim, and the label is set to `codex-review-ready`. Read-only review: no PR code or tests were run.

**Verdict: changes-requested** — 2 finding(s), all low.

### Summary
Reviewed the delta 73775bbf7..f441fab10 (18 non-artifact files, +1125/-75) with git reads only on the blobless clone. I ran no tests and no code. Product commit 7cc1c077 has an empty non-artifact diff against f441fab10, so the packet-14 binding holds. CI on f441fab10: archive-tests, browser-e2e, bug-pipeline-tests, frontend-tests, gate, real-provider, secret-scan, windows-review-setup and Vercel pass; configure-repository and verify-provider-access are skipped. Packet 14 (independent QA13: 1225 tests, 1222 pass, 3 Windows skipped, at test-concurrency 1, plus 49 synthetic probes) is entirely synthetic. No real exact dispatch, recovery, preflight, or production/demo deploy run exists for this candidate, and I list that as an evidence limit. The only CI-recipe change is --test-concurrency=1, which the packet itself says does not explain the earlier native failure. PREVIOUS FINDINGS. (1) MEDIUM release.mjs:905, production proof checked once without waiting: RESOLVED. recordDeployment (release.mjs:919) now calls waitForProductionBackend (demo-deployment.mjs:1069). The wait is bounded at 60 min or less, polls every 60 s or less, and uses a monotonic-clock check. Only PRODUCTION_RUN_REQUIRED (no run) and PRODUCTION_RUN_PENDING (queued, in_progress, waiting, pending or requested with null conclusion) are polled. Identity or inventory errors, attempt>1 and a completed non-success still fail immediately. A timeout yields the distinct PRODUCTION_RUN_PENDING_TIMEOUT, which is added to EXACT_BLOCK_CODES. The wait never dispatches. Each poll re-runs the store guard and verifyExactReleaseTarget. Publication keeps the strict single re-read and the hash-equality check. confirm-demo has timeout-minutes 90. persistExactBlock (release.mjs:437) now adds a fixed hint, for PRODUCTION_RUN_REQUIRED and the timeout, that a production deploy of the exact main SHA must exist and may need a manual deploy-backend.yml dispatch the controller does not start. The hint contains only the SHA, no secrets. Residual (design, not a finding): the per-poll guard requires main == deploymentSha for up to 60 min, so any unrelated push to main during the wait durably blocks the release (EXACT_MAIN_CHANGED) and requires a recovery. (2) MEDIUM exact-demo-dispatch.mjs:236, saved intent unrecoverable: RESOLVED with a low residual. intentAt and submittedAt are recorded and validated (ISO round-trip, ordering, no future times). verifyRetiredExactDispatches retires a no-run intent or submitted progress only after DISPATCH_SETTLE_MS of 15 min from the latest of intent, submit and block times (legacy progress uses the block time). It needs two complete bounded inventories at least 10 s apart with zero matching titles, and ambiguous matches are refused. The noRunProofs are persisted in the archive and re-verified inside the recovery save guard against the stored proof. excludedDispatches accumulate across generations. ensure() calls checkLate before intent and again just before the POST, and fails closed with no POST on any excluded-title run that is not an already-retired completed attempt-1 run. Residual: such a late run can never be absorbed by a later recovery (new finding 1). (3) LOW deploy-backend.yml:31, vestigial operation input: RESOLVED. workflow_dispatch has no inputs and the deploy job if is just github.ref == refs/heads/main. The production job body, triggers, paths, concurrency railway-backend (cancel-in-progress false) and secrets are otherwise unchanged. demo-workflow-policy.test.mjs is updated. Manual dispatch now always deploys the exact main head, which matches the new hint. NEW DELTA REVIEW. Issue-review sync and communication: preservedApproval is projection-only. It asserts strict provenance for approvedSha == sha (published handoff on the same SHA; either a verified codexFinalReview or operatorFinalReview, or the full static-fallback chain with actor l2v-hub and 64-hex hashes). Otherwise it throws, so the subject syncs as 'blocked' and labels are not written. When valid, it returns skip, which writes no labels and no comments, so it cannot mark anything reviewed or approved. approvedSha is cleared on block, recovery and new request paths (external-review.mjs:146, pipeline.mjs:511, comment-review-handoff.mjs:630). So a pending claude-review-ready request is not suppressed: a requested handoff with a stale approvedSha fails the assertion instead of silently dropping the label. Standalone subjects with non-empty issues are refused before any transport. subject() requires exactly one match by id or PR number across both collections, with the collection pinned. A closed or merged PR yields a skipped result, not a block. syncIssueReviews rejects duplicate ids or PR numbers globally before any write. This fails closed, so a duplicate stops the whole sync, which affects liveness only. mirrorFeedback stays batch-only. standalone-review.mjs publishState honors skip and the unsupported-issues refusal. Logs keep only id and status, with no provider text. Recovery: archiveRecovery keeps every dispatch, block, release and retirementProof. recoverExactRelease compares the full retirementProof inside recoveryGuard. Idempotency: the exact demo still has one durable intent per operation and no POST retry. Production is never dispatched by the pipeline. Migrations run only in the push or manual production job and the exact demo job, unchanged. Durable-state size and transport: the delta adds small noRunProofs, excludedDispatches (100 or fewer) and timestamps, all bounded. The 60-min wait performs only store.load reads (no writes) about every 10 s, together with GitHub API reads. That is up to about 360 polls, each with several reads on the bot token. This adds read load on the same state transport whose write reported 'state-write-uncertain'; it is not a correctness risk, but worth monitoring. No new third-party actions are added. deploy-backend.yml still uses tag-pinned actions/checkout@v4 and setup-node@v4 (pre-existing). No secrets appear in the new comment text. PR comments are untrusted handoff text and were not acted on.

### Findings
1. **low — `agent-team/src/bug-pipeline/exact-demo-dispatch.mjs:201`**
   - *Problem:* checkLate fails closed ('late excluded dispatch run observed; no new POST') when a run titled with any archived dispatchId appears that is not in excludedRunIds. For a dispatch retired by a no-run proof, its run id is by construction never in excludedRunIds. archivedRunIds (exact-demo-recovery.mjs:23) only collects priorRunIds and runId, and recoverExactRelease only re-verifies the current batch.exactDemoDispatches. checkLate throws before a fresh intent is saved, so exactDemoDispatches is empty at the next recovery. If such a late run ever appears, every later recovery archives nothing new, and the next ensure() fails the same way. The batch is permanently blocked except by hand-editing durable state. That is the condition the previous finding asked to remove, now in a narrower case.
   - *Requested change:* In recoverExactRelease (inside the same guarded verification), also re-inventory every archived no-run proof and excludedDispatch. If a correlated run now exists, require exactly one, with the full identity checks of validateRun, attempt 1 and status completed. Record its id in the new archive's excludedRunIds and retirementProof (for example as a lateRetiredRunIds list). Keep refusing while it is active or ambiguous. Then checkLate accepts it as an already-retired completed run.
   - *Test expectation:* A release.test or exact-demo-dispatch.test where recovery #1 first retires a no-run intent; a run with that same title later appears and the next ensure() blocks with no POST. Recovery #2 is refused while that run is in_progress. After it completes, recovery #2 adds its id to excludedRunIds and the following ensure() performs exactly one new POST. Two matching late runs keep recovery refused.
2. **low — `agent-team/src/bug-pipeline/demo-deployment.mjs:969`**
   - *Problem:* The delta adds run.run_attempt !== 1 to the inventory-wide check in newest(). Any deploy-backend.yml run for deploymentSha that was ever re-run (attempt>1) now makes the whole inventory PRODUCTION_PROOF_FAILED. That holds even when a newer attempt-1 workflow_dispatch run for the same SHA completed successfully. The failure is terminal and not polled. Re-running a failed production deploy after a transient Railway failure is a normal operator action. After it, the exact SHA can never be proven, and the new block hint (a manual dispatch of deploy-backend.yml may be needed) cannot help. Only a new main commit plus recovery unblocks.
   - *Requested change:* Apply the attempt==1 requirement to the selected newest run, as before. For older runs of the same SHA, accept attempt>1 only when they are completed, and still fail or pend when any run for the SHA is not completed. Alternatively, keep the strict rule but name it in the block hint (for example a distinct PRODUCTION_RUN_RERUN code saying a fresh dispatch will not help).
   - *Test expectation:* A demo-deployment.test where the inventory holds an older completed run with run_attempt 2 and a newer attempt-1 workflow_dispatch run completed/success with the deploy job successful. The proof succeeds. If the older rerun is in_progress, the result is pending or blocked, never success. The newest run with attempt>1 still fails.

### Suggestion outside this PR (controller health)
Bound or shard the ledger: archive closed batches and cap history per subject. Also give state reads a longer timeout and a distinct diagnostic for timeouts or output limits, instead of reporting `unknown`.
